metadata.case_name: LAM YIM FONG v. ADVARA INVESTMENT LTD

plaintiff.occupation_before: Cashier of a money exchange company (Kinying Renminbi Exchange Co)
plaintiff.education_level: Secondary education in Hong Kong with little vocational training

source: The experts agree that the plaintiff had a mild head injury at the time when she was hit by the fallen signboard.

injuries.description: right shoulder injury (pain and decreased movement; no fracture on X-ray)
source: the defendant accepts that the plaintiff was hit by the signboard at her right shoulder and sustained injuries
the plaintiff complained of "right shoulder pain and decrease in movement".
An X-ray examination did not reveal any fracture.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of shoulder joint

injuries.description: vasovagal syncope (episode of dizziness and loss of consciousness for five minutes)
source: she was discharged on 15 June 2010 with a diagnosis of vasovagal syncope.

manifestations.description: On and off headache described as like being jabbed by many needles; frequency ranges from every second day to 3 to 4 times a month, each bout lasting half a day to a few days
Dizziness / vertigo (including episodes after accident and induced by Barany maneuver)
Memory impairment (difficulty memorising a new telephone number, cannot keep a shopping list in mind, may forget where she has placed her belongings)
Persistent neck and right shoulder pain and stiffness, increasing after sleep or with rainy and windy weather
Episode of loss of consciousness for five minutes followed by sleepiness
Moderate degree of diffuse give-way weakness in the right arm

treatments_received: Accident and Emergency treatment at Queen Elizabeth Hospital
CT scan of brain (no abnormality revealed)
Admission to Neurosurgical Ward of the Prince of Wales Hospital
Treatment by bone setters and herbalist

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Contribution to domestic chores is limited because such duty as mopping the floor would induce vertigo.
Memory impairment affecting ability to memorise new information and daily tasks.
Temper has worsened; she scolds her family members often.
Will have some difficulties coping with jobs which are mentally or physically demanding, will need more time to find suitable employment and may have significant periods of unemployment in future.
